intent.raw_query: Istanbul cultural exploration, $1800 solo, historical sites and cuisine, May 2026

experiences.name: Hagia Sophia & Blue Mosque Exploration
experiences.description: Spend a morning exploring the iconic Hagia Sophia, a UNESCO World Heritage Site that has served as a cathedral, mosque, and museum over its 1,500-year history. Walk across Sultanahmet Square to the stunning Blue Mosque, admiring its six minarets and intricate Iznik tile interior. Hire a local guide for deeper historical context on Byzantine and Ottoman empires.

experiences.name: Grand Bazaar & Spice Bazaar Food and Shopping Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the Grand Bazaar, one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops. Continue to the Egyptian Spice Bazaar to sample Turkish delight, saffron, dried fruits, and local spices. Interact with vendors, practice bargaining, and taste free samples of authentic Turkish flavors along the way.

experiences.name: Topkapi Palace & Harem Tour
experiences.description: Explore the magnificent Topkapi Palace, the administrative heart of the Ottoman Empire for nearly 400 years. Walk through the Imperial Treasury, view sacred relics, and take a guided tour of the Harem quarters to uncover the private lives of sultans and their court. The palace grounds also offer panoramic views of the Bosphorus strait.

experiences.name: Traditional Turkish Breakfast & Bosphorus Ferry Cruise
experiences.description: Start the day with a lavish Turkish breakfast (kahvaltı) featuring olives, white cheese, simit, eggs, honey, and fresh tea at a local café in Karaköy. Afterward, board a public Bosphorus ferry for a scenic cruise between Europe and Asia, passing Ottoman palaces, wooden yalı mansions, and ancient fortresses along the shoreline.

experiences.name: Balık Ekmek, Meyhane Dinner & Istiklal Street Night Walk
experiences.description: Begin the evening with a famous balık ekmek (grilled fish sandwich) from the floating boats near Galata Bridge. Stroll across the iconic bridge watching fishermen at dusk, then head to a traditional meyhane (tavern) in Beyoğlu for a feast of meze dishes, grilled lamb, and raki. End the night exploring the vibrant Istiklal Avenue with its historic tram, street musicians, and lively atmosphere.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Istanbul
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Istanbul Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect baggage. Take the Havaist airport bus or metro to minimize transport costs (approx. 50-80 TRY vs. 400+ TRY for a taxi). Check into Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront area. Freshen up and settle into your room.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack near the hotel — look for a 24-hour büfe (corner shop) for a simit (sesame bread ring) or a quick döner wrap for under 50 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Keep all receipts from airport transport for budget tracking. Exchange a small amount of cash (USD/EUR to TRY) at the airport for immediate needs — avoid dynamic currency conversion. Save bulk exchange for city center banks or ATMs for better rates.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast if included, or walk to a nearby local bakery for a traditional Turkish breakfast (kahvaltı) — tea, olives, cheese, tomatoes, cucumber, and bread for around 80-120 TRY. Explore the immediate beachfront neighborhood on foot to get your bearings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Sultanahmet historic district (accessible by tram or ferry depending on hotel location). Visit the iconic Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya) — now a mosque with free entry. Admire the stunning Byzantine mosaics, massive dome, and centuries of layered history. Dress modestly and bring a headscarf if needed (available free at entrance).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the Sultanahmet Square and view the exterior of the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque) illuminated at dusk — a magical sight. Walk along the Hippodrome of Constantinople to see the Obelisk of Theodosius and the Serpent Column for free. Return to hotel area.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery or hotel — simit, tea, and cheese for 80-120 TRY
meals.lunch: Sultanahmet Köftecisi — one of Istanbul's oldest köfte (meatball) restaurants near the square. A plate of köfte with bread and ayran costs around 150-200 TRY
meals.dinner: Local neighborhood pideci (Turkish flatbread restaurant) near the hotel — a pide with cheese or meat topping costs 100-150 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Purchase an Istanbulkart (rechargeable transit card) for 70 TRY — it gives significant discounts on all public transport including trams, buses, ferries, and metro. Essential for budget travel in Istanbul.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque) in the morning when it's less crowded — free entry but closed during prayer times (check schedule). Spend time inside admiring the 20,000 blue Iznik tiles and six minarets. Then walk five minutes to the Topkapi Palace — the heart of the Ottoman Empire for 400 years. Entry around 200-300 TRY.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Topkapi Palace — visit the Imperial Treasury, the Harem (separate ticket ~150 TRY), and the kitchens housing Chinese porcelain collections. The palace grounds offer stunning views over the Bosphorus and Golden Horn. Spend 3-4 hours here easily.
day_by_day.evening: Walk down to the Eminönü waterfront. Buy a famous balık ekmek (fish sandwich) from the floating boats moored at the docks — an Istanbul institution for around 60-80 TRY. Watch the sunset over the Golden Horn. Take the tram or ferry back to your hotel area.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or a local çay bahçesi (tea garden) — Turkish tea and pastry for 50-80 TRY
meals.lunch: Topkapi Palace cafeteria or bring packed snacks to save money — simit from a street cart for 10-15 TRY
meals.dinner: Balık ekmek at Eminönü waterfront (60-80 TRY) plus a cup of çay (tea) from a nearby tea vendor for 10 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Topkapi Palace is closed on Tuesdays — plan accordingly. The Harem is a must-see for history lovers. Arrive early to beat tour groups. Wear comfortable walking shoes as the palace grounds are extensive.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) — one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops. Free entry. Explore the labyrinthine lanes selling spices, carpets, jewelry, ceramics, and leather goods. Practice the art of bargaining — prices are always negotiable. Open Mon-Sat from 8:30am.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 10 minutes to the Egyptian Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) — a feast for the senses with colorful spices, Turkish delight, dried fruits, and nuts. Buy small quantities of spices or lokum (Turkish delight) as affordable souvenirs. Then stroll along the bustling Mahmutpaşa market street for an authentic local shopping experience.
day_by_day.evening: Cross the Galata Bridge on foot — fishermen line the bridge day and night. Walk up to the Galata Tower area in Karaköy. Climb the medieval Galata Tower for panoramic city views (entry ~150 TRY) or admire it from outside for free. Explore the hip Karaköy neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or street simit cart near the Grand Bazaar — simit with tea for 20-30 TRY
meals.lunch: Eat at a local esnaf lokantası (workers' restaurant) near the bazaar — a full meal of soup, main course, and bread for 100-150 TRY. These no-frills restaurants serve home-style Turkish cooking at very affordable prices
meals.dinner: Karaköy Güllüoğlu — a legendary baklava shop in Karaköy. Enjoy a portion of fresh baklava with tea for 80-120 TRY as a light, indulgent dinner treat, or grab a cheap pide nearby

day_by_day.notes: The Grand Bazaar is closed on Sundays. Beware of overly friendly strangers who offer to show you around — a common setup for overpriced carpet shops. Keep your belongings secure in crowded market areas.

day_by_day.morning: Take a short Bosphorus ferry (public ferry via Istanbulkart — only 20-30 TRY, far cheaper than tourist cruises) from Eminönü to Üsküdar on the Asian side. Enjoy stunning views of palaces, mosques, and the iconic skyline. Explore Üsküdar's traditional neighborhood, visit the Mihrimah Sultan Mosque, and see the famous Maiden's Tower (Kız Kulesi) from the shore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the ferry back to the European side or continue to explore the Asian shore. Visit Kadıköy — Istanbul's vibrant, bohemian neighborhood on the Asian side. Explore the Kadıköy market (Kadıköy Çarşısı) with its fresh produce, fish, and specialty food shops. Browse the independent bookshops, vintage stores, and street art.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the lively evening atmosphere in Kadıköy. The neighborhood has a young, local energy with street musicians and affordable bars. Take the ferry back to Eminönü as the sun sets over the Bosphorus — one of Istanbul's most beautiful free experiences.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or grab a börek (flaky pastry with cheese or spinach) from a Üsküdar bakery — 40-60 TRY
meals.lunch: Kadıköy market area — try kokoreç (grilled offal sandwich, a local delicacy) for 60-80 TRY or fresh mussels stuffed with rice (midye dolma) from street vendors at 10-15 TRY each
meals.dinner: A meyhane (traditional Turkish tavern) in Kadıköy — share meze plates (small appetizers) with bread and ayran for around 150-200 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: The public Bosphorus ferry is one of Istanbul's best budget experiences. Avoid the tourist 'Bosphorus cruise' boats at Eminönü which cost 5-10x more for a similar experience. Keep your Istanbulkart handy for ferry rides.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Istanbul Archaeology Museums (İstanbul Arkeoloji Müzeleri) — a complex of three museums near Topkapi Palace housing over one million artifacts including the Alexander Sarcophagus. Entry around 150-200 TRY — extraordinary value. Spend 2-3 hours here exploring ancient civilizations from across the region.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Süleymaniye Mosque — the grandest mosque in Istanbul, built by Suleiman the Magnificent in the 16th century. Free entry. Climb to the surrounding streets of the Süleymaniye neighborhood for sweeping views over the Golden Horn. Explore the quiet, atmospheric streets of this historic hilltop district.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the Beyazıt neighborhood and visit the Beyazıt Mosque (free). Walk through the Istanbul University gate area and down to the Sahaflar Çarşısı (second-hand book bazaar) — a peaceful, atmospheric spot even in the evening. Head back via tram.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or a local kahvaltı salonu (breakfast salon) near Sultanahmet — full Turkish breakfast spread for 120-180 TRY
meals.lunch: Süleymaniye area has excellent cheap restaurants catering to students and locals — try Tarihi Süleymaniye Kurufasülyecisi for a bowl of kuru fasülye (white bean stew) with rice and bread for 80-100 TRY, a true Istanbul classic
meals.dinner: Beyazıt area lokanta — soup, main, and bread for 100-150 TRY

day_by_day.notes: The Süleymaniye Mosque is less touristy than the Blue Mosque but equally impressive. The surrounding neighborhood is one of the best-preserved historic areas in Istanbul and perfect for photography. The archaeology museum is underrated and well worth the entry fee.

day_by_day.morning: Take the tram to Kabataş and walk up to Taksim Square — the modern heart of Istanbul. Explore İstiklal Avenue (İstiklal Caddesi), a 1.4km pedestrian boulevard lined with historic buildings, churches, embassies, bookshops, cafes, and street performers. Ride the nostalgic red tram that runs along the avenue (Istanbulkart accepted).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Beyoğlu neighborhood's side streets off İstiklal — Çiçek Pasajı (Flower Passage), the Balık Pazarı (fish market), and the atmospheric Nevizade Sokak. Visit the Church of St. Anthony of Padua (free) — one of Istanbul's largest Catholic churches. Explore the Pera neighborhood with its Art Nouveau architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Pera Museum (Pera Müzesi) — entry around 100-150 TRY — for its famous Orientalist paintings collection including Osman Hamdi Bey's 'The Tortoise Trainer.' Afterward, enjoy the buzzing evening atmosphere of Beyoğlu's bars and cafes.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or a Taksim area pastane (pastry shop) — tea and a slice of börek for 50-80 TRY
meals.lunch: Balık Pazarı area — a plate of fresh fried fish with bread and salad at a standing fish restaurant for 100-150 TRY
meals.dinner: Nevizade Sokak — a lively street of meyhanes. Order a selection of cold meze (hummus, cacık, patlıcan salatası) and a main for around 200-250 TRY. Avoid tourist-facing restaurants; go where locals are seated

day_by_day.notes: İstiklal Avenue can be very crowded on weekends. The side streets are where the real character of Beyoğlu lives. Keep an eye on your belongings in the busy pedestrian areas. Many museums offer free entry on the first Sunday of the month — check dates.

day_by_day.morning: Take a ferry from Kabataş or Beşiktaş to Ortaköy — a charming waterfront neighborhood at the foot of the Bosphorus Bridge. Visit the ornate Ortaköy Mosque right on the waterfront. Ortaköy is famous for its Sunday market with crafts and antiques — great for browsing without pressure to buy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue up the European shore of the Bosphorus by bus or dolmuş (shared minibus) to Bebek — one of Istanbul's most affluent and beautiful neighborhoods. Walk along the Bebek waterfront promenade. Visit Rumeli Hisarı (Rumelian Castle) — a massive 15th-century fortress built by Mehmed II before the conquest of Constantinople. Entry around 50-80 TRY.
day_by_day.evening: Take a bus back toward Beşiktaş — a lively, working-class neighborhood with excellent street food and local atmosphere. Explore the Beşiktaş market area and the waterfront. Take the ferry or bus back to your hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or buy a kumpir (giant stuffed baked potato) in Ortaköy — the neighborhood is famous for them — for 100-150 TRY
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from a local market — bread, cheese, tomatoes, olives, and fruit for under 100 TRY. Eat by the Bosphorus in Bebek
meals.dinner: Beşiktaş street food — try a midye dolma (stuffed mussel) crawl along the waterfront at 10-15 TRY each, plus a tavuk döner (chicken döner) for 80-100 TRY

day_by_day.notes: The Bosphorus shore bus routes (25E, 40) are very affordable with Istanbulkart. Rumeli Hisarı is a hidden gem that most tourists skip — the views from the towers over the Bosphorus are spectacular. Wear sturdy shoes for the castle's uneven cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Chora Church (Kariye Mosque/Museum) — a Byzantine masterpiece containing some of the finest surviving Byzantine mosaics and frescoes in the world, dating from the 14th century. Located in the Edirnekapı neighborhood. Entry around 100-150 TRY. Arrive early to avoid crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the ancient Theodosian Walls (Land Walls of Constantinople) — the 5th-century walls that protected the city for a thousand years. Stretching 6.5km, you can walk a section for free. Visit the Edirnekapı (Adrianople Gate) area. Explore the colorful, authentic Fatih neighborhood — one of Istanbul's most traditional and conservative districts.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Fener and Balat neighborhoods — two of Istanbul's most atmospheric and photogenic historic areas along the Golden Horn. Wander the steep, colorful streets with Ottoman-era wooden houses. Visit the Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople (free, check visiting hours). Watch the Golden Horn light up at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or a Fatih neighborhood bakery — freshly baked bread and cheese for 60-80 TRY
meals.lunch: A Fatih lokanta — this conservative neighborhood has excellent, cheap, authentic Turkish food. A full meal for 100-120 TRY
meals.dinner: Balat area has several charming cafes and small restaurants popular with young locals and expats. A meal in a Balat bistro for 150-200 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Balat and Fener are rapidly gentrifying but still retain enormous character. The colorful houses make for excellent photography. Dress modestly in Fatih out of respect for the conservative local community. The Chora Church is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and absolutely unmissable for history lovers.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı) — a stunning 6th-century underground water cistern with 336 columns, atmospheric lighting, and the famous Medusa head column bases. Entry around 200 TRY but worth every kuruş. Open early — arrive when it opens to experience the eerie beauty without crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Cemberlitas Hammam — one of Istanbul's oldest and most beautiful Turkish baths, designed by the legendary architect Sinan in 1584. A basic bath and scrub experience starts around 400-500 TRY — a splurge but a once-in-a-lifetime cultural experience. Alternatively, find a local neighborhood hammam for 150-200 TRY for a more authentic, less touristy experience.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening after the hammam. Stroll through Sultanahmet as the day-trippers leave and the neighborhood becomes more peaceful. Visit the Arasta Bazaar — a quieter, less aggressive alternative to the Grand Bazaar — for last-minute souvenir shopping. Watch the Blue Mosque's evening lighting.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or Sultanahmet area café — menemen (Turkish scrambled eggs with tomatoes and peppers) for 80-100 TRY
meals.lunch: Tarihi Sultanahmet Köftecisi — the historic köfte restaurant near the Hippodrome, a landmark since 1920. Köfte, bread, and ayran for 150-200 TRY
meals.dinner: A relaxed meal at a neighborhood restaurant away from the main tourist strip — ask hotel staff for their recommendation. Budget 150-200 TRY for a filling meal

day_by_day.notes: The Basilica Cistern recently expanded with new sections — it's larger than most visitors expect. Book the hammam in advance if possible, especially on weekends. The Cemberlitas Hammam is tourist-oriented but historically significant; for a more local experience, ask your hotel to recommend a neighborhood hammam.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to the Princes' Islands (Adalar) — a group of nine car-free islands in the Sea of Marmara. Take the public ferry from Kabataş terminal (Istanbulkart, around 40-60 TRY each way). The largest island, Büyükada, is 90 minutes away. Explore the island by horse-drawn carriage (phaeton) or rent a bicycle for 100-150 TRY for the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle or ride around Büyükada's pine-forested hills, passing grand Victorian-era wooden mansions. Hike up to the Monastery of St. George on the hilltop for panoramic views over the Marmara Sea. The island has a wonderfully peaceful, time-capsule atmosphere far removed from Istanbul's chaos.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry to Istanbul in the late afternoon/early evening. Enjoy the sea breeze and views of Istanbul's skyline as you approach the city. Have a relaxed dinner near your hotel to recover from the day's walking.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or grab something at Kabataş ferry terminal before boarding
meals.lunch: Büyükada has several fish restaurants along the waterfront — a grilled fish plate with salad and bread for 200-250 TRY. Or bring a packed lunch from Istanbul to save money
meals.dinner: Neighborhood restaurant near hotel — a simple, filling meal for 120-150 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Ferries to the Princes' Islands are very popular on weekends — go on a weekday if possible to avoid crowds. Check the IDO or Şehir Hatları ferry schedules in advance. Bring sunscreen and a hat as the island has little shade. The islands are one of Istanbul's most beloved escapes and a highlight of any visit.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Istanbul Modern (İstanbul Modern) — Turkey's first modern art museum, relocated to a stunning new building in Karaköy designed by Renzo Piano. Entry around 150-200 TRY. Explore contemporary Turkish art and rotating international exhibitions. The building itself, with its Bosphorus views, is worth the visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Karaköy and Tophane neighborhoods — a creative hub with galleries, design shops, and cafes. Visit the Tophane-i Amire Culture and Arts Center (often free exhibitions). Walk along the waterfront to Fındıklı and up to Cihangir — a bohemian hillside neighborhood beloved by artists, writers, and expats, with charming cafes and antique shops.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening splurge — visit a rooftop bar or restaurant in Beyoğlu for sunset views over the Bosphorus and Golden Horn. Many offer affordable drinks and meze. Alternatively, take an evening walk across the Galata Bridge and enjoy the atmosphere of fishermen, street vendors, and the illuminated mosques.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or a Cihangir café — avocado toast and coffee is popular here but look for traditional alternatives for better value. Budget 100-150 TRY
meals.lunch: Karaköy street food — a fresh lahmacun (thin Turkish pizza with minced meat) rolled with parsley and lemon for 40-60 TRY, or a portion of çiğ köfte (spiced bulgur rolls) for 30-50 TRY
meals.dinner: A mid-range meyhane in Beyoğlu for a celebratory last proper dinner — meze, grilled fish or kebab, and dessert for 250-350 TRY. This is a budget splurge but worth it for the final evening

day_by_day.notes: Istanbul Modern is closed on Mondays. Cihangir is one of Istanbul's most livable and photogenic neighborhoods — perfect for a slow, wandering afternoon. The rooftop bars along İstiklal and Beyoğlu offer spectacular views; look for happy hour deals to keep costs down.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a final Turkish breakfast — either at the hotel or at a local neighborhood kahvaltı spot. Pack and check out. Take a final short walk along the beachfront area near the hotel to soak in the last views. Pick up any last-minute souvenirs — Turkish tea (çay), spices from the Spice Bazaar (if you bought any earlier), or lokum (Turkish delight) make excellent budget-friendly gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the airport with plenty of time. Use the Havaist bus or metro with your Istanbulkart for an affordable airport transfer. Arrive at least 2.5-3 hours before your flight for international departures. You can top up or refund the remaining balance on your Istanbulkart at the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Istanbul. Reflect on 13 incredible days of history, culture, and food in one of the world's greatest cities.

meals.breakfast: Final Turkish breakfast — menemen, çay, simit, and cheese at a local spot for 100-150 TRY
meals.lunch: Airport food (budget accordingly — airport prices are higher) or eat before departing from a city restaurant for 100-150 TRY
meals.dinner: On the plane

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary tips: Istanbulkart saved significant money on all transport. Eating at lokanta and street food vendors kept daily food costs to 200-400 TRY. Many of Istanbul's greatest sights (mosques, markets, waterfront walks, neighborhoods) are completely free. The city rewards slow, curious exploration on foot more than any other approach. Total estimated daily budget (excluding accommodation): 400-700 TRY per day for food, transport, and entry fees.

trip_options.title: Classic Istanbul Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Istanbul Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange airport transfer (pre-booked taxi or Havaist airport bus) to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront district. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with the hotel amenities.

meals.breakfast: N/A – In-flight meal
meals.lunch: N/A – In-flight meal
meals.dinner: Light late-night snack at the hotel or a nearby 24-hour café if available upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light – no scheduled activities. Pre-download offline maps (Google Maps or Maps.me) for Istanbul. Exchange a small amount of currency at the airport for immediate expenses. Confirm hotel transfer in advance to avoid delays at 22:30.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. After resting from travel, take a gentle orientation walk along the Beachfront promenade near the Aegean Bliss Resort to get your bearings, enjoy the sea air, and explore the immediate neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearby Princes' Islands (Adalar) ferry terminal if accessible from the Beachfront area, or explore the local seaside district. Browse local shops, pick up a SIM card, and visit a neighborhood market to sample fresh produce and local snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at a local meyhane (traditional Turkish tavern) near the hotel. Try classic meze dishes such as hummus, ezme, stuffed grape leaves, and grilled fish.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort – enjoy Turkish staples like simit, olives, white cheese, tomatoes, cucumbers, and tea
meals.lunch: Casual neighborhood lokanta (traditional Turkish cafeteria-style restaurant) – try lentil soup, stuffed peppers, and ayran
meals.dinner: Local meyhane near the hotel – meze spread with raki or fresh fruit juice, grilled sea bass or bream (approx. 300–500 TL per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is a recovery and orientation day. Don't over-schedule. Purchase an Istanbul Kart (transit card) from a nearby kiosk for easy access to ferries, trams, and buses throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Sultanahmet, Istanbul's historic heart. Begin with the Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya-i Kebir Camii) – arrive early (opens at 09:00) to beat the crowds. Marvel at the Byzantine mosaics, massive dome, and the blend of Christian and Islamic heritage. Spend 1.5–2 hours inside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 5 minutes to the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Camii). Admire the six minarets and stunning Iznik tile interior. Note: mosque is closed to tourists during prayer times, so time your visit accordingly. Afterward, explore the Hippodrome of Constantinople (Sultanahmet Square) and see the Obelisk of Theodosius and the Serpent Column.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the Arasta Bazaar adjacent to the Blue Mosque for quality Turkish handicrafts without the Grand Bazaar crowds. Enjoy dinner in Sultanahmet with views of illuminated historic monuments.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Tarihi Sultanahmet Köftecisi – iconic meatball restaurant near the Hippodrome; try the classic köfte with white beans and fresh bread (budget-friendly, approx. 150–200 TL)
meals.dinner: Matbah Restaurant or a similar mid-range Ottoman cuisine restaurant in Sultanahmet – try Ottoman-inspired dishes like hünkârbeğendi (lamb on eggplant purée) and baklava for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Wear modest clothing for mosque visits (cover shoulders and knees; women bring a headscarf). The Hagia Sophia is free to enter but may require a timed entry reservation – check ahead. Sultanahmet is easily reached by tram (T1 line, Sultanahmet stop).

day_by_day.morning: Visit Topkapi Palace (Topkapı Sarayı) – the opulent residence of Ottoman sultans for 400 years. Explore the Imperial Treasury (home to the Topkapi Dagger and Spoonmaker's Diamond), the Harem (separate ticket required), and the Sacred Relics section. Allow 3–4 hours minimum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk downhill through Gülhane Park to the Istanbul Archaeological Museums (Arkeoloji Müzeleri) – a world-class complex housing the Alexander Sarcophagus, the Treaty of Kadesh (world's oldest peace treaty), and artifacts spanning 5,000 years of civilization. Allow 2 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Take the tram or taxi to the Eminönü waterfront. Watch the sunset over the Golden Horn, then cross the Galata Bridge on foot. Enjoy the lively atmosphere of fishermen casting lines from the bridge. Explore Karaköy neighborhood below Galata Tower.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Konyalı Restaurant inside Topkapi Palace grounds – a historic institution serving traditional Turkish cuisine with Bosphorus views (mid-range, approx. 300–400 TL)
meals.dinner: Karaköy Güllüoğlu (famous baklava shop) for dessert, preceded by a fish sandwich (balık ekmek) from a boat vendor at Eminönü – a quintessential Istanbul street food experience (approx. 100–150 TL)

day_by_day.notes: Topkapi Palace is closed on Tuesdays – if this is indeed a Tuesday, swap Day 4 and Day 5 activities. Purchase combined tickets where possible. The Archaeological Museums are underrated and often uncrowded – a hidden gem.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) – one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops. Navigate the labyrinthine lanes of jewelry, carpets, spices, ceramics, and leather goods. Practice your bargaining skills. Opens at 09:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 10 minutes to the Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) in Eminönü. Sample Turkish delight, dried fruits, nuts, saffron, and herbal teas. Purchase local spices and sweets as souvenirs. Afterward, take a short Bosphorus ferry ride from Eminönü to Üsküdar on the Asian side for a unique perspective of the city.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Üsküdar on the Asian side of Istanbul. Visit the Mihrimah Sultan Mosque and the charming Kız Kulesi (Maiden's Tower) visible from the shore. Enjoy dinner in Üsküdar's authentic local neighborhood, less touristy than the European side.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Havuzlu Restaurant inside the Grand Bazaar – a classic mid-range option beloved by locals and traders (try lamb stew and Turkish bread, approx. 250–350 TL)
meals.dinner: Kanaat Lokantası in Üsküdar – a legendary traditional restaurant open since 1933, serving home-style Turkish food like braised lamb, stuffed eggplant, and rice pudding (approx. 200–300 TL)

day_by_day.notes: The Grand Bazaar is closed on Sundays. Arrive early (before 10:00) to avoid peak crowds. Keep valuables secure in busy market areas. The Eminönü–Üsküdar ferry costs just a few TL with your Istanbul Kart and offers stunning views.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Süleymaniye Mosque (Süleymaniye Camii) – Sinan's masterpiece and the largest mosque in Istanbul, offering panoramic views over the Golden Horn. Wander through the surrounding historic külliye (mosque complex) with its medrese, hamam, and tombs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend into the Balat and Fener neighborhoods – two of Istanbul's most atmospheric and photogenic historic districts. Wander colorful Ottoman-era houses, visit the Greek Orthodox Patriarchate (Ekümenik Patrikane), and explore the Chora Church (Kariye Camii) with its extraordinary Byzantine mosaics and frescoes (check restoration status ahead of visit).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the European side and explore the vibrant Beyoğlu district. Walk the famous İstiklal Avenue (İstiklal Caddesi) and ride the historic Tünel funicular. Explore side streets filled with art galleries, vintage shops, and live music venues.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Balat's local eateries – try a neighborhood börek shop or a small lokanta for gözleme (stuffed flatbread), menemen (Turkish scrambled eggs with tomatoes), and fresh ayran (approx. 100–200 TL)
meals.dinner: Beyoğlu meyhane on Nevizade Sokak – a famous alley of taverns serving meze, fresh fish, and cold Efes beer or raki in a lively social atmosphere (approx. 350–500 TL)

day_by_day.notes: Balat is best explored on foot – wear comfortable shoes as the streets are cobblestoned and hilly. The neighborhood has become increasingly popular with photographers and Instagram travelers, so morning visits offer a more authentic experience.

day_by_day.morning: Take a full Bosphorus Cruise – board the public ferry from Eminönü or Beşiktaş for the classic long Bosphorus tour (approx. 2.5 hours each way). Sail past Dolmabahçe Palace, Rumeli Fortress, Yıldız Palace, and the stunning Bosphorus Bridge. Disembark at Anadolu Kavağı on the Asian shore.
day_by_day.afternoon: At Anadolu Kavağı, hike up to the ruined Byzantine/Genoese Yoros Castle for spectacular views where the Bosphorus meets the Black Sea. Browse the small fishing village, then board the return ferry back to Eminönü.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Galata Tower (Galata Kulesi) at dusk for 360-degree panoramic views over Istanbul, the Bosphorus, and the Golden Horn. The tower is especially magical at sunset. Afterward, explore the hip Karaköy and Galata neighborhoods.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast (early start recommended to catch the 10:35 morning ferry)
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish lunch at one of the seafood restaurants at Anadolu Kavağı village – try grilled sea bream, calamari, and meze (approx. 300–450 TL, negotiate set menus)
meals.dinner: Karaköy neighborhood dinner – try Gram Restaurant or a similar modern Turkish bistro in the area for contemporary takes on Turkish cuisine (approx. 350–500 TL)

day_by_day.notes: The public Bosphorus ferry (IDO/BUDO lines) is far more authentic and affordable than private tour boats. Check the official BUDO ferry schedule ahead of time as departures are limited. The full round trip takes most of the day – bring sunscreen, a hat, and a light jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Dolmabahçe Palace (Dolmabahçe Sarayı) in Beşiktaş – the lavish 19th-century Ottoman palace where Atatürk spent his final days. Marvel at the 4.5-ton Bohemian crystal chandelier (the world's largest), gilded halls, and stunning Bosphorus-facing façade. Book guided tours in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Beşiktaş neighborhood and its lively Saturday market. Walk or take a taxi to the Çırağan Palace (now a luxury hotel) to admire its exterior along the Bosphorus. Visit the Yıldız Park (Yıldız Parkı) – a beautifully landscaped Ottoman imperial park perfect for a relaxing afternoon stroll.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the upscale Nişantaşı neighborhood for an evening of window shopping along Abdi İpekçi Street and Teşvikiye Avenue. Enjoy dinner at one of the neighborhood's stylish mid-range restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Beşiktaş market area – try a fresh simit with cheese and tea, or grab a döner from a reputable local spot (approx. 80–150 TL)
meals.dinner: Nişantaşı restaurant – try Sunset Grill & Bar or a similar venue offering modern Turkish-Mediterranean cuisine with quality ingredients (approx. 400–600 TL)

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace requires a timed guided tour ticket – book online in advance, especially on weekends. The palace is closed on Mondays and Thursdays. Photography is restricted in certain interior sections.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Edirne (optional) or explore the Fatih district deeply. If staying in Istanbul: visit the Fatih Mosque (Fatih Camii), the Zeyrek Mosque (a converted Byzantine church), and the historic Vefa neighborhood. Alternatively, visit the Istanbul Museum of the History of Science and Technology in Islam.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Eyüp Sultan district – one of Istanbul's most sacred Islamic sites. Visit the Eyüp Sultan Mosque and the historic cemetery. Take the Pierre Loti Cable Car (teleferik) up to the hilltop Pierre Loti Café for stunning views over the Golden Horn while sipping Turkish coffee.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Beyoğlu area and explore the Cihangir neighborhood – a bohemian, artsy district beloved by Istanbul's creative class. Browse antique shops, independent bookstores, and cozy cafés.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Pierre Loti Café on the hilltop – enjoy Turkish coffee, tea, and light snacks with panoramic Golden Horn views (approx. 100–200 TL)
meals.dinner: Cihangir neighborhood restaurant – try Cuma Restaurant or a local bistro serving modern Anatolian cuisine in a relaxed, neighborhood atmosphere (approx. 300–450 TL)

day_by_day.notes: Eyüp Sultan is a deeply religious neighborhood – dress modestly. The Pierre Loti Café is a historic institution named after the French novelist who frequented it. Sunday is a great day for Cihangir as the neighborhood comes alive with locals.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı) – Istanbul's magnificent underground Byzantine cistern dating to the 6th century AD. Marvel at the forest of 336 marble columns, atmospheric lighting, and the famous Medusa head column bases. Then visit the nearby Mosaic Museum (Büyük Saray Mozaikleri Müzesi).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Küçük Ayasofya Mosque (formerly the Church of Saints Sergius and Bacchus) – a proto-Byzantine church predating Hagia Sophia and often called 'Little Hagia Sophia.' Wander the quiet streets of the Kadırga and Kumkapı neighborhoods along the Marmara Sea coast.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Kumkapı – Istanbul's famous fish restaurant district along the Marmara coast. This lively neighborhood is packed with meyhanes and seafood restaurants with live fasıl music (traditional Ottoman classical music performed by roving musicians).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Sultanahmet area – try Cooking Alaturka for a hands-on Turkish cooking class lunch experience, or dine at a traditional lokanta with daily specials (approx. 200–300 TL)
meals.dinner: Kumkapı meyhane – enjoy a full seafood feast with meze, grilled fish, and live fasıl music. Negotiate a set menu price before sitting down (approx. 400–600 TL including music)

day_by_day.notes: The Basilica Cistern underwent major renovations and reopened with a new visitor experience – book tickets online to avoid queues. Kumkapı is lively and touristy in the evenings but offers an authentic Istanbul night out – be prepared for persistent but good-natured restaurant touts.

day_by_day.morning: Cross to the Asian side of Istanbul for a full day of exploration. Take the ferry from Eminönü or Karaköy to Kadıköy – Istanbul's vibrant, youthful Asian neighborhood. Explore the Kadıköy Market (Tarihi Kadıköy Çarşısı) – a wonderful covered food market bursting with local cheeses, olives, pickles, fresh produce, and street food.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Moda neighborhood adjacent to Kadıköy – a charming seaside district with tree-lined streets, Art Nouveau architecture, independent cafés, and a relaxed local vibe. Walk the Moda coastline and enjoy views of the Princes' Islands and the European skyline across the water.
day_by_day.evening: Take the ferry to Büyükada (Princes' Islands) for a magical evening excursion, or return to the European side via ferry for dinner. If staying in Kadıköy, enjoy dinner in one of the neighborhood's excellent local restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Kadıköy Market food tour – graze on local specialties: kokoreç (offal sandwich), midye dolma (stuffed mussels), fresh börek, and sample cheeses and pickles at market stalls (approx. 150–250 TL)
meals.dinner: Çiya Sofrası in Kadıköy – a legendary restaurant celebrated internationally for its authentic Anatolian regional cuisine, rotating daily menus, and rare Ottoman recipes. A must-visit for food lovers (approx. 250–400 TL)

day_by_day.notes: Çiya Sofrası is one of Istanbul's most acclaimed restaurants – arrive early or expect a wait. The Kadıköy Market is best visited in the morning when it's freshest. The Asian side feels noticeably different from the European side – more local, less touristy, and very authentic.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Princes' Islands (Adalar) – take the morning ferry from Kabataş or Eminönü to Büyükada, the largest of the nine islands. Rent a bicycle or hire a horse-drawn phaeton carriage (fayton) to explore the car-free island. Visit the Monastery of St. George on the hilltop for panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax on one of Büyükada's small beaches or explore the island's charming Victorian-era wooden mansions and pine forests. Enjoy the peaceful, unhurried atmosphere – a complete contrast to the urban intensity of Istanbul.
day_by_day.evening: Return by ferry to Istanbul in the late afternoon. Spend your last full evening exploring the Galata and Karaköy neighborhoods. Visit a traditional Turkish hamam (bathhouse) for a classic hammam experience – try Kılıç Ali Paşa Hamamı in Karaköy (mid-range, approx. 600–900 TL for full treatment).

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at hotel before early ferry departure
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at a restaurant on Büyükada – fresh grilled fish, calamari, and meze with Marmara Sea views (approx. 300–450 TL)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a special Istanbul restaurant – try Mikla Restaurant (rooftop, modern Turkish cuisine with panoramic city views) for a memorable final dinner (approx. 600–900 TL, reservation essential)

day_by_day.notes: Check the ferry schedule carefully – ferries to the Princes' Islands can be crowded on weekends. The round trip takes about 1.5–2 hours each way. Book the hamam in advance as popular spots fill up quickly. Mikla requires a reservation – book at least 1–2 weeks ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Istanbul. Enjoy a leisurely last hotel breakfast. If time permits before checkout, take a final walk along the Beachfront promenade near the Aegean Bliss Resort. Visit any remaining sights near the hotel or pick up last-minute souvenirs from a local shop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Depending on your departure flight time, store luggage at the hotel and make one final visit to a neighborhood you loved, or head directly to Istanbul Airport. Allow 2–3 hours before departure for airport check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Istanbul. Reflect on 13 wonderful days of history, culture, and incredible food.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast – savor the full Turkish breakfast spread one last time
meals.lunch: Airport lunch or a quick stop at a neighborhood café near the hotel for a final Turkish tea and simit before heading to the airport
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining

day_by_day.notes: Istanbul Airport (IST) is approximately 45–60 minutes from the city center by taxi or Havaist bus (longer during rush hour). Budget extra time. Use any remaining Turkish Lira at the airport or exchange back to your home currency. Keep your Istanbul Kart as a souvenir or return it at a kiosk for a small deposit refund.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Istanbul Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Istanbul Airport on Flight UA at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check-in, unwind with a welcome drink at the hotel bar, and enjoy a light late-night room service spread.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Late-night in-room dining: mezze platter, Turkish cheese board, and herbal tea from the resort's 24-hour kitchen

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer with the hotel concierge. Request early check-in amenities such as chilled towels, Turkish delight, and Bosphorus-view room if available.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely start with a lavish breakfast at the resort's terrace restaurant overlooking the Bosphorus. Afterward, take a private guided orientation walk along the beachfront promenade to acclimate to the surroundings and enjoy sea views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided visit to the Topkapi Palace — explore the Imperial Treasury, Harem quarters, and sacred relics with an expert historian guide. Enjoy exclusive access arrangements through the concierge.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar in Sultanahmet, followed by a private dinner at Tugra Restaurant inside Çırağan Palace Kempinski, offering Ottoman imperial cuisine with Bosphorus panoramas.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort terrace — full Turkish breakfast with simit, olives, white cheese, honey, clotted cream, fresh pastries, and eggs cooked to order
meals.lunch: Light mezze lunch at a café near Topkapi Palace — stuffed vine leaves, hummus, grilled flatbread
meals.dinner: Tugra Restaurant at Çırağan Palace Kempinski — tasting menu featuring Ottoman-inspired dishes such as lamb tandir, sea bass in saffron sauce, and baklava soufflé

day_by_day.notes: Book Topkapi Palace skip-the-line tickets and private guide in advance. Tugra Restaurant reservation should be made at least one week ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Hagia Sophia — explore the Byzantine mosaics, grand dome, and rich layered history with a specialist art historian. Arrive early to beat crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through the Sultanahmet Hippodrome and visit the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque). Then head to the nearby Arasta Bazaar for a curated luxury shopping experience — hand-woven kilims, ceramic art, and fine Turkish textiles.
day_by_day.evening: Private Bosphorus dinner cruise aboard a chartered yacht — enjoy live classical Turkish music, a multi-course dinner, and illuminated views of the city skyline, bridges, and waterfront palaces.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — freshly squeezed pomegranate juice, menemen (Turkish scrambled eggs with tomatoes and peppers), börek, and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Matbah Restaurant near Sultanahmet — Ottoman palace recipes including lentil soup, stuffed quince, and lamb with dried apricots
meals.dinner: Private yacht dinner cruise — lobster bisque, grilled sea bream, Ottoman-spiced lamb chops, and Turkish dessert selection with Bosphorus views

day_by_day.notes: Modest dress required for Blue Mosque (head covering and shoe removal). Book the private yacht charter through the hotel concierge at least 3 days in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive private tour of the Grand Bazaar with a cultural guide — discover the history of the 4,000+ shop labyrinth, learn about traditional craftsmanship, and visit master artisan workshops for gold jewelry, hand-painted ceramics, and silk carpets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Spice Bazaar (Egyptian Bazaar) for a sensory immersion in Turkish flavors. Participate in a premium private Turkish cooking class at a nearby culinary studio — learn to prepare manti, imam bayildi, and kunefe.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Nicole Restaurant in Tomtom Suites — Michelin-recognized contemporary Turkish cuisine with a seasonal tasting menu and panoramic Golden Horn views.

meals.breakfast: Resort — açma (soft Turkish roll), clotted cream, fig jam, Turkish tea, and a made-to-order omelette station
meals.lunch: Dishes prepared during the cooking class served as lunch in the culinary studio
meals.dinner: Nicole Restaurant — contemporary tasting menu with wine pairing, featuring innovative takes on classic Anatolian ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private carpet consultation at a reputable dealer in the Grand Bazaar if interested in purchasing. Cooking class should be booked 48 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the Basilica Cistern — explore the atmospheric underground Byzantine water reservoir with its Medusa columns and atmospheric lighting. Then visit the Istanbul Archaeology Museums for a world-class collection of antiquities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross to the Asian side of Istanbul via a private Bosphorus ferry. Explore the charming Kadıköy neighborhood — stroll through the vibrant market, visit local spice shops, and browse independent bookstores and galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Çiya Sofrası in Kadıköy — a legendary restaurant celebrated for preserving rare Anatolian recipes from across Turkey, followed by a return ferry ride with evening city lights.

meals.breakfast: Resort terrace — Turkish simit with sesame, local honey, aged tulum cheese, soft-boiled eggs, and fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Kadıköy market lunch — grilled fish sandwich (balık ekmek), stuffed mussels (midye dolma), and fresh ayran
meals.dinner: Çiya Sofrası — rotating seasonal menu of rare regional Turkish dishes including slow-cooked meats, fermented vegetable stews, and heritage grain pilafs

day_by_day.notes: The Kadıköy market is most vibrant on weekday mornings. Çiya Sofrası is extremely popular — arrive early or ask the hotel to call ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Indulge in a traditional hammam experience at the historic Çemberlitaş Hamamı (built 1584) — enjoy a private kese (exfoliation scrub), foam massage, and relaxation in the marble steam room.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided tour of the Süleymaniye Mosque complex — explore the grand Ottoman architecture, the mausoleum of Suleiman the Magnificent, and the surrounding historic neighborhood of Eminönü.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along the Galata Bridge followed by dinner at Mikla Restaurant atop the Marmara Pera Hotel — panoramic 360-degree rooftop views and award-winning New Anatolian cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Resort — full spread with pastırma (cured beef), kaymak (clotted cream) with honey, freshly baked poğaça, and Turkish coffee
meals.lunch: Darüzziyafe Restaurant in the Süleymaniye complex — Ottoman-era recipes in a beautifully restored soup kitchen setting
meals.dinner: Mikla Restaurant — New Anatolian tasting menu with Aegean herbs, Black Sea fish, and Anatolian wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book the hammam private suite in advance for a more exclusive experience. Mikla Restaurant is one of Istanbul's most celebrated — reservation essential.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Dolmabahçe Palace — the opulent 19th-century Ottoman imperial residence on the Bosphorus shore, featuring 285 rooms, crystal staircases, and the world's largest Bohemian crystal chandelier.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the upscale Nişantaşı neighborhood — Istanbul's answer to Paris's 8th arrondissement. Browse luxury Turkish fashion boutiques, contemporary art galleries, and designer concept stores.
day_by_day.evening: Private dinner at Feriye Lokantası in Ortaköy — a beautifully converted 19th-century Ottoman police station on the Bosphorus, serving refined Ottoman and Turkish cuisine with waterfront views.

meals.breakfast: Resort — eggs Benedict with Turkish sucuk (sausage), freshly baked bread, seasonal fruit platter, and freshly brewed Turkish coffee
meals.lunch: Nişantaşı café lunch — seasonal salads, gourmet Turkish flatbreads, and artisan desserts at a chic patisserie
meals.dinner: Feriye Lokantası — Bosphorus-view dining with dishes such as sea bass ceviche with pomegranate, slow-roasted lamb shoulder, and Ottoman rose milk pudding

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace requires advance ticket booking and has a dress code. Photography restrictions apply in certain palace rooms.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to the Princes' Islands (Adalar) — take a private boat charter to Büyükada, the largest island. Explore by horse-drawn carriage, visit the Monastery of Saint George, and enjoy the peaceful, car-free atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Büyükada — swim at a private beach club, stroll through the Victorian-era wooden mansions, and enjoy the island's slower pace of life away from the city bustle.
day_by_day.evening: Return by private boat to Istanbul at sunset. Dinner at Seasons Restaurant at the Four Seasons Sultanahmet — elegant Mediterranean-Turkish cuisine in a converted 19th-century prison turned luxury hotel.

meals.breakfast: Resort — light continental spread with pastries, fruit, and coffee before early departure
meals.lunch: Büyükada island lunch at a waterfront restaurant — fresh grilled fish, calamari, and island salads with local white wine
meals.dinner: Seasons Restaurant, Four Seasons Sultanahmet — refined tasting menu with Aegean seafood, Anatolian lamb, and artisan Turkish desserts

day_by_day.notes: Private boat charter to the Princes' Islands should be arranged 2-3 days in advance. Bring sun protection as the island has limited shade. The islands are most beautiful in spring.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Chora Church (Kariye Mosque) — home to some of the world's finest Byzantine mosaics and frescoes. Then explore the historic Fener and Balat neighborhoods — colorful Ottoman-era Greek and Jewish quarters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Phanar Greek Orthodox Patriarchate and explore the atmospheric streets of Balat with its antique shops, vintage markets, and street art. Participate in a private calligraphy workshop with a master Ottoman calligrapher.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Karaköy Lokantası in the Karaköy district — a beloved institution serving elevated traditional Turkish meyhane cuisine in a beautifully tiled space.

meals.breakfast: Resort — menemen with fresh herbs, simit with sesame, local jams, and a selection of Turkish teas
meals.lunch: Balat neighborhood lunch at a local meyhane — cold and hot mezze including arnavut ciğeri (Albanian-style liver), tarama, and grilled halloumi
meals.dinner: Karaköy Lokantası — sharing-style mezze dinner with cold and hot starters, whole grilled fish, and homemade desserts

day_by_day.notes: The Chora Church may have restricted access depending on ongoing restoration work — confirm with the hotel concierge before visiting. Balat is best explored on foot.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the Pera Museum in Beyoğlu — home to the famous 'Tortoise Trainer' painting by Osman Hamdi Bey and an outstanding collection of Orientalist art, Anatolian weights, and Kütahya tiles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the vibrant Beyoğlu district — stroll along İstiklal Avenue, visit the historic Pera Palace Hotel (where Agatha Christie wrote 'Murder on the Orient Express'), and browse the Çiçek Pasajı (Flower Passage) arcade.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private Whirling Dervishes (Sema) ceremony at a historic tekke, followed by dinner at Asitane Restaurant — the gold standard for Ottoman imperial cuisine, using recipes from the Topkapi Palace kitchens.

meals.breakfast: Resort — full Turkish spread with a focus on Aegean specialties: wild herbs, olive varieties, and fresh local cheese
meals.lunch: Beyoğlu patisserie lunch — premium börek, gözleme (stuffed flatbread), and traditional Turkish desserts at Hafız Mustafa 1864
meals.dinner: Asitane Restaurant — Ottoman imperial tasting menu featuring dishes such as almond soup, stuffed melon, and rose water desserts from 15th-century palace recipes

day_by_day.notes: Private Whirling Dervishes ceremonies can be arranged through the hotel concierge for a more intimate and authentic experience than public tourist shows. Asitane requires advance reservation.

day_by_day.morning: Private full-day Bosphorus yacht tour — cruise northward along the European and Asian shores, stopping at Rumeli Fortress (Rumelihisarı), the charming village of Anadolu Kavağı, and the mouth of the Black Sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Bosphorus cruise southward — admire the yalıs (wooden Ottoman waterfront mansions), pass under the Bosphorus Bridge, and stop at Bebek for a coffee break at the famous Bebek Kahve.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by private yacht at sunset. Farewell pre-dinner cocktails at the resort's beachfront bar, followed by a premium dinner at the resort's signature restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Resort — champagne breakfast on the terrace before departure for the yacht
meals.lunch: Onboard yacht catered lunch — fresh seafood mezze, grilled fish, Turkish salads, and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort signature restaurant — premium tasting menu featuring Aegean and Bosphorus-inspired dishes with locally sourced ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Full-day private yacht charter should be booked 4-5 days in advance. Bring layers as the Bosphorus breeze can be cool even in May. Sunscreen essential.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the Istanbul Modern Art Museum (recently reopened in its stunning new building) — explore contemporary Turkish and international art with a specialist art guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the fashionable Karaköy and Galata neighborhoods — visit the Galata Tower for panoramic city views, browse independent design boutiques and artisan studios, and visit the Galata Mevlevi Lodge Museum.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell gala dinner at Sunset Grill & Bar in Ulus — one of Istanbul's most prestigious restaurants with sweeping Bosphorus views, an award-winning wine cellar, and contemporary Turkish-international cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Resort — lavish final morning spread with all Turkish breakfast classics, freshly baked goods, and made-to-order eggs
meals.lunch: Karaköy lunch at Namlı Gurme — a legendary deli and restaurant serving premium Turkish charcuterie, artisan cheeses, and freshly prepared mezze
meals.dinner: Sunset Grill & Bar — premium tasting menu with Bosphorus sunset views, featuring dry-aged meats, Aegean seafood, and an extensive Turkish and international wine list

day_by_day.notes: The Istanbul Modern has ticketed entry — book online in advance. Sunset Grill & Bar is extremely popular at sunset; request a window table when booking.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely morning at the resort — enjoy a slow breakfast, take a last swim or spa treatment, and pack at your own pace. Optional: a final walk along the beachfront promenade to soak in the last views of the Bosphorus.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time — optional last-minute visit to a nearby artisan shop or patisserie for final souvenir purchases (Turkish delight, premium teas, hand-painted ceramics). Private luxury transfer to Istanbul Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. The hotel concierge can arrange VIP airport lounge access and private check-in assistance.

meals.breakfast: Resort — final full Turkish breakfast with all favorites: fresh pastries, local cheeses, honey, eggs, and Turkish coffee
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at the resort or airport VIP lounge depending on departure time
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Request a late checkout from the hotel to maximize your final morning. Arrange private airport transfer at least 3 hours before departure. Pack purchased Turkish goods carefully — ceramics and glassware are fragile.

query: Istanbul cultural exploration, $1800 solo, historical sites and cuisine, May 2026
